submission.justification: Sensor-T2 is excluded: after 2e16 neq/cm^2 its hit efficiency is 82.0%, far below the >=97% end-of-life requirement, due to strong charge trapping. Of the two remaining radiation-tolerant options, Sensor-T3 (planar) gives better unirradiated single-hit resolution than Sensor-T1 (3D) at every thickness simulated. Simulated T3 resolution: 10.0 um at 50 um, 9.4 um at 100 um, 8.9 um at 150 um, 9.5 um at 200 um. Sensor-T1 ranged from 14.1 to 16.2 um. 150 um gave the best T3 resolution among the points tested, and it is within the 50-300 um range. Sensor-T3 measured 98.5% efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2, meeting the requirement. Caveat: the irradiation result is not tied to a specific thickness in the document, and the resolutions are unirradiated, so post-irradiation resolution at 150 um was not simulated.

requirements.requirement: Sensor must be one of the three candidate technologies
Suitable for innermost-layer radiation environment (>=97% hit efficiency at end of life, 2e16 neq/cm^2)
requirements.evidence: irradiation_testbeam_2026.md: Sensor-T3 98.5% after 2e16 neq/cm^2. Sensor-T2 (82.0%) and Sensor-T1 (99.2%) were considered separately; T2 fails.

Simulated unirradiated resolution: T3 8.93 um at 150 um, the best of the points tested (T3 9.4 um at 100 um, 9.5 um at 200 um, 10.0 um at 50 um). Sensor-T1 14.1-16.2 um; Sensor-T2 6.0 um at 150 um (2025 summary) but fails the radiation requirement.
